title: Reciprocal polynomial of a polynomial with constant term one
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P(T)=\sum_{k=0}^{r}c_kT^k\in R[T]$ with $c_0=P(0)=1$ and $c_r\neq0$, so that $r=\deg P$. Define the reciprocal polynomial

$$
P^\#(U)=U^{r}P(U^{-1}):=\sum_{k=0}^{r}c_kU^{r-k}\in R[U].
$$

Then:

1. $P^\#$ is monic of degree $r$, and $P^\#(0)=c_r$.
2. Let $\varphi:R\to K$ be a ring homomorphism into a field $K$ with $\varphi(c_r)\neq0$ (for instance any injective $\varphi$; for $R=\mathbf Z$, the unique homomorphism into any field $K$ of characteristic $0$), and write $\varphi(Q)$ for the coefficientwise extension of $Q\in R[T]$. Then $\deg\varphi(P)=r$, $\varphi(P)(0)=1$, and $\varphi(P^\#)=(\varphi(P))^\#$.
3. For $\varphi$ as in (2) and $x\in K$: $\varphi(P^\#)(x)=0$ if and only if $x\neq0$ and $\varphi(P)(x^{-1})=0$. Equivalently, $\varphi(P^\#)(x)=x^{r}\,\varphi(P)(x^{-1})$ for $x\neq0$, and $\varphi(P^\#)(0)=\varphi(c_r)\neq0$. In particular the roots of $\varphi(P^\#)$ in $K$ are exactly the inverses of the roots of $\varphi(P)$ in $K$, and all of them are nonzero.
